notes: Reconciled four-PR review stack: 241 literal native registrations, 232 OpenAPI operations, eight explicitly documented media-protocol surfaces and one internal lease callback. No unassigned residual registrations.

OpenAPI coverage includes JSON, binary downloads and other explicitly described responses. The eight media-protocol registrations remain outside the projected OpenAPI document; partial=true preserves that distinction.
Discovery is descriptive. Every request must independently satisfy current principal, token, action, resource and deployment checks. Inventory coverage never grants access.
Historical slices and their counts are retained in execution receipts, not repeated as current coverage. The original baseline had 57 accepted operations out of 240 registrations.
F3 administration: 20 operations; Basic/legacy-key compatibility remains, while scoped users.manage cannot issue unrestricted legacy keys.
F4 fleet writes/workspaces: 31 operations; owner, revision, selectors and actual PNG/JPEG background bytes are independently tested.
F5/F6 storage: 28 operations; scheduling acknowledgments do not prove asynchronous file completion. Local lifecycle evidence does not qualify remote providers.
F7 system/settings/bootstrap: 23 operations; owned process/backup effects, credential masks, zero values and snapshot-bound bootstrap discovery are tested.
F8 events: 13 operations; owned MQTT packet, retry and suppression evidence is separate from JSON acknowledgments.
F9/F10: 15 stream lifecycle JSON operations, 22 ONVIF/device operations and eight explicit protocol dispositions. Owned media/SOAP evidence does not qualify physical cameras or multicast discovery.
F11 evidence: 23 operations; captured UUID is authoritative where present, legacy identity fallback is explicitly bounded, and media/image/CSV bytes have independent evidence.
See engineering-hardening-four-pr-plan.md and docs/api/contracts/*-evidence.md for accepted behavior, exact validation and remaining limitations.
